text:
Andrew: quick RFC follow-up — we need to settle the interface between the rate-limiter and the abuse-scoring service. do we call the scorer synchronously during admission or defer and apply penalties async?
Maria: prefer async for p99 latency but worried about correctness for short-lived bursts (spam). can we do hybrid?
Jess: hybrid sounds right — fast path: local heuristic + token-bucket admit, offload to scorer for post-hoc penalties. if scorer flags, we retroactively escalate penalties for a tenant.
Rahul: agreed. two tradeoffs: 1) sync gives immediately correct admits but adds latency on every request. 2) async keeps latency low but we need strong compensating controls (short windows, reversible penalties).
Kate: operational concerns — how do we surface "retro-penalties" to UX? we shouldn't silently drop customer traffic. maybe we throttle with warnings and send audit events.
Andrew: good point. proposal: 
- admission flow: local adapter -> token-bucket check -> admit.
- emit event to abuse-queue with sample keys. scorer consumes, returns score.
- if score > threshold, update admission policy for that tenant for N minutes (penalty window).
Jess: sample payload idea: `{ tenant_id, route, recent_rps, sketch_counts }` so scorer can make informed decision without full request stream.
Maria: for the token-bucket config we should support a per-tenant elasticity factor. example config snippet: 
```
{
  capacity: 200,
  refill_tokens_per_sec: 50,
  elasticity: 0.5  // multiplies refill when tenant has high quality signals
}
```
Rahul: where do we store penalty state? central config store vs local cache? central store gives correctness but single point of failure. local cache keeps fast checks but eventual consistency required.
Kate: hybrid again — central store for authoritative state, local LRU cache with TTL=30s for hot tenants. update via pubsub so changes propagate quickly.
Andrew: scoring latency SLO: scorer should process 99% of events < 500ms, but we won't block requests on that. penalty propagation SLO: 99% of updates reach local caches within 5s.
Jess: metrics to track: pre/post admission delta, number of retro-penalties, false positives (customer tickets), score distribution, action latency. add a dashboard + alert on FP rate > 1% over 1h.
Maria: one more thing — abuse evasion patterns (multi-tenant churn) mean we should fingerprint behavioral clusters, not only tenant id. scorer should emit cluster_id so router can apply cluster-level caps.
Rahul: implementation notes: use a compact sketch (count-min + time-decayed) in events. scorer can correlate across routes. keep event payload <= 2KB.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline: abuse-scorer v2 to canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC, rollback 09:30 if error-rate > 0.5% on critical routes.
Kate: i'll own rollout and dashboarding. Andrew — can you own the RFC update with the hybrid flow and interfaces (/admit, /events, /penalty) so we can ship next week?
Andrew: yep, i'll update the RFC with diagrams and an example event schema. tagging folks for review: @Maria @Jess @Rahul @Kate. :thumbsup:
Maria: ack, will review today.
Jess: will add unit tests for local heuristic and penalty application.
Rahul: i'll prototype the sketch encoder.
Kate: thanks — will coordinate canary.
Andrew: closing notes — we aim to avoid blocking the client path, keep event size small, and ensure transparent penalties. follow-up sync Wed 10am PT.
